newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. poll finds high approval for Giuliani.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. poll finds high approval for Giuliani.

text.p: Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's approval rating was at an all-time high among New York voters, who favour him over all potential Democratic challengers in this year's election, according to a poll released Thursday.

But the poll by Quinnipiac College in Hamden, Connecticut, also showed most voters do not like the tough-talking Republican mayor very much. Only 44 percent told the pollsters Giuliani had a "likeable personality" even though 67 percent approve of the job he is doing.
The poll surveyed 901 New York City residents, who say they are registered voters, March 19-25. The poll has a margin of error of plus or minus three percent.
A survey by the same college in February showed Giuliani's approval rating at 62 percent with 52 percent saying they did not like him personally.
The new poll showed New Yorkers by a margin of 52 to 25 percent approved of Giuliani's decision this month to appear on stage dressed as a woman.

"Are New Yorkers seeing a kindler, gentler, more likeable Rudolph Giuliani? His overall job rating is at another peak," Maurice Carroll, director of the Quinnipiac College Polling Institute, said in a statement. "It's up only a few points over the peak the last time but his numbers are so lofty it's hard to move more than a few points."
Giuliani was still way ahead of the four politicians who will compete in September's Democratic Party primary to find a candidate to challenge the incumbent mayor, the poll found.

He leads closest challenger Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messinger by 50 percent to 38 percent; Bronx Borough President Fernando Ferrer by 51 percent to 35 percent; City Councilman Sal Albanese by 57 to 24 percent and black activist Al Sharpton by 66 to 19 percent.
Giuliani's lead in the polls over Messinger narrowed to 12 percent from 20 percent since the Feb. 11 poll, which was taken when former Mayor David Dinkins was considering a run.
The mayor won high marks for his handling of crime -- 82 percent approval -- but less than half approved of the way he was handling education, the poll found.
